subject: History
unitTitle: Peoples, States and Historical Processes in Ethiopia and the Horn to the End of the 13th Century

questions.question: Which of the following African language super-families has the widest geographical distribution in northern, central, northeastern Africa and the Horn?

options.text: Niger-Congo
Khoisan
Nilo-Saharan
Afro-Asiatic

questions.explanation: Afro-Asiatic is the most important super-family in terms of geographical distribution in northern, central, northeastern Africa and the Horn, comprising Cushitic, Omotic, Semitic, Berber, Chadic, and ancient Egyptian families.

questions.question: Which ancient commercial port on the western coast of the Red Sea served as the primary maritime outlet for the Kingdom of Aksum according to the 'Periplus of the Erythraean Sea'?

options.text: Avalites (Zeila)
Adulis
Malao (Berbera)
Serapion (Mogadishu)

questions.explanation: According to the 1st-century travel guide 'Periplus of the Erythraean Sea', Adulis on the western coast of the Red Sea served as the primary port and maritime gateway of the Aksumite state.

questions.question: Who was consecrated by Patriarch Athanasius of Alexandria as the first Christian bishop of the Kingdom of Aksum in the 4th century A.D.?

options.text: Abba Aregawi
Abba Minas
Frumentius
Saint Yared

questions.explanation: Frumentius, credited with converting King Ezana to Christianity in the 4th century A.D., traveled to Alexandria where Patriarch Athanasius consecrated him as the first bishop (Abuna) of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church.

questions.question: Which local ruling dynasty founded the medieval Zagwe dynasty around the middle of the twelfth century?

options.text: The Walasma dynasty of Ifat
The Agaw of Wag and Lasta under Mera Tekle Haymanot
The Makhzumite clan of eastern Shewa
The Minjo royal clan of Kafa

questions.explanation: The Zagwe dynasty was founded in the mid-12th century by Mera Tekle Haymanot, an Agaw general from Lasta married to the daughter of the last Aksumite king, Dil Na'od.

questions.question: In the indigenous Waqefanna religion of the Oromo people, who serves as the spiritual father and leader whose ceremonial anointment (Jila) provides nationwide blessings?

options.text: Abba Muda
Abbaa Duulaa
Abbaa Bokku
Abba Sera

questions.explanation: In Oromo indigenous religion, Abba Muda is the supreme spiritual leader to whom pilgrims from various Oromo confederacies travel during the sacred Jila pilgrimage to receive blessings and anointments of righteousness.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a branch of the Cushitic language family with its representative languages spoken in Ethiopia and the Horn?

options.text: North Cushitic — Shinasha and South Ma'o
Central Cushitic (Agaw) — Bilen, Qimant, Hamtang, and Awgni
Lowland East Cushitic — Hadiya, Kambata, Sidama, and Gedeo
Highland East Cushitic — Afan Oromo, Afar, and Somali

questions.explanation: Central Cushitic (also called Agaw languages) comprises Bilen (in Eritrea), Hamtang, Qimant, and Awgni; Shinasha is Omotic, while Hadiya and Sidama are Highland East Cushitic, and Afan Oromo and Somali are Lowland East Cushitic.

questions.question: What archaeological evidence from the pre-Aksumite state of Da'amat confirms its advanced metallurgical technology, sedentary agricultural economy, and external maritime trade?

options.text: Manufacture of iron tools and weapons, millet cultivation, and exchange of gold, ivory, and slaves with South Arabian merchants through Yeha
Large-scale coin mintage in bronze and silver bearing Sabaean script discovered at Sof Omar
Extensive monolithic rock-hewn basilicas built from soft limestone in the Awash Valley
Construction of terraced hydraulic canals along the Blue Nile to export frankincense to Meroe

questions.explanation: The Kingdom of Da'amat (c. 980–400 B.C.), centered at Yeha, produced iron tools and weapons, cultivated millet, and conducted active trade in gold, silver, ivory, and tortoise shells with South Arabian merchants.

questions.question: How did internal and external long-distance commercial exchange operate between Aksum and the region of Sasu as recorded in Cosmas Indicopleustes' 'Christian Topography'?

options.text: Through standardized gold coin auctions conducted by Alexandrian consular brokers
Via silent barter trade where Aksumite merchants exchanged cattle, iron, and salt blocks for gold without verbal negotiation
By direct military confiscation of gold mines along the Omo River basin
Through royal maritime flotillas operating across the Gulf of Aden to Ceylon

questions.explanation: The Adulis inscription recorded in Cosmas' 'Christian Topography' documents a large caravan of royal Aksumite traders traveling to Sasu (in present-day Benishangul) who conducted 'silent trade' by leaving cattle, salt blocks, and iron to be exchanged for gold without direct contact.

questions.question: What primary military motivation led King Kaleb of Aksum (r. c. 500–535 A.D.) to launch an overseas naval expedition across the Red Sea into South Arabia?

options.text: To conquer the Persian Sassanid capital of Ctesiphon with Byzantine naval support
To defeat the Jewish ruler Dhu-Nuwas, who had persecuted Christians in Zafar and Najran, and restore Aksumite hegemony over Himyar and Saba
To seize commercial monopolies over the trans-Saharan caravan network in Meroe
To secure exclusive possession of the Dahlak Islands against Arab pirates

questions.explanation: King Kaleb crossed the Red Sea with Byzantine assistance to defeat Dhu-Nuwas, a South Arabian prince converted to Judaism who had massacred Christians in Najran and Zafar, subsequently appointing Abreha as governor of the South Arabian province.

questions.question: What major socio-cultural and ecclesiastical contributions are attributed to the Nine Saints who arrived in the Aksumite kingdom from the Eastern Roman Empire in the late 5th century?

options.text: They minted the first gold coins bearing the sign of the cross and built the defensive ditch of Hiriyoo
They expanded monastic institutions, introduced church architecture resembling Syrian basilicas, and translated the Holy Bible into Ge'ez
They established the Council of Boru Meda and outlawed the practice of ritual ablution
They formulated the Fitha Negest civil code and negotiated the 42nd Pseudo-Canon with Alexandria

questions.explanation: The Nine Saints founded monasteries (such as Debre Damo), spread Christianity among the broader rural populace, influenced church architecture, and translated Biblical scriptures into the Ge'ez language.

questions.question: What was the political fate of the Muslim Sultanate of Shewa in 1285 A.D.?

options.text: It was conquered and incorporated by the rising Walasma dynasty of the neighboring Sultanate of Ifat
It formed an unbroken confederation with the Kingdom of Damot to overthrow the Zagwe dynasty
It was partitioned between the Mamluk Sultanate of Egypt and the Dahlak Sultanate
Its Makhzumite ruling family was peacefully restored to the throne of Aksum

questions.explanation: In 1285 A.D., the Makhzumite dynasty of Shewa was overthrown and annexed by Umar Walasma, the founder of the Sultanate of Ifat, terminating the existence of the Sultanate of Shewa as an independent polity.

questions.question: Which combination of internal and external factors brought about the economic decline and eventual political collapse of the Aksumite Empire?

options.text: The Portuguese naval blockade of Massawa combined with large-scale peasant uprisings in Gojjam

Arab Muslim destruction of Adulis (c. 702 A.D.) and control of Red Sea trade routes, alongside environmental degradation, agricultural decline, and rebellions by the Beja, Agaw, and Queen Bani al-Hamwiyah (Yodit)
The complete annexation of northern Tigray by the Mamluk armies of Egypt
The total exhaustion of iron deposits in Yeha and the northward migration of the Oromo

questions.explanation: Aksum's international trade artery was cut when Arab Muslims destroyed the port of Adulis around 702 A.D. and took control of Red Sea commerce; this external isolation combined with environmental degradation, declining soil fertility, and recurring internal revolts by the Beja, Agaw, and Queen Yodit to cause its collapse.

questions.question: What religious and geopolitical motivation inspired King Lalibela and other Zagwe monarchs to undertake the monumental construction of the rock-hewn monolithic churches at Roha?

options.text: To establish a 'second Jerusalem' in the Ethiopian highlands after Muslim Arab control of the Red Sea and Egypt made traditional pilgrimages to the Holy Land hazardous for Ethiopian Christians
To replace the Patriarchate of Alexandria with an independent indigenous papacy in Lasta
To shelter royal gold treasuries from expanding naval raids by the Ottoman Empire
To celebrate the military defeat of the Solomonic restoration movement in Shewa

questions.explanation: Because Muslim control over the Middle East and Red Sea made Christian pilgrimages to Jerusalem perilous, Zagwe rulers—especially King Lalibela—embarked on building the rock-hewn churches at Roha (Adafa) to replicate the holy sites as a 'second Jerusalem' on Ethiopian soil.

questions.question: How did the royal succession dispute within the Zagwe dynasty interact with the ideological narrative of the 'Kibre Negest' to bring about its downfall in 1270 A.D.?

options.text: Rival Agaw princes invited the Mamluks to arbitrate dynastic legitimacy at Debre Damo

Internal succession feuds weakened Zagwe authority, enabling Yekuno Amlak of Amhara to rally influential church leaders like Abune Tekle Haymanot and depose King Yetbarek by claiming legitimate descent from King Solomon and Queen Sheba through the Aksumite line
The Council of Nicea invalidated Zagwe monastic land holdings due to Greek liturgy
The Zagwe rulers converted to Islam, prompting an excommunication by the Patriarch of Alexandria

questions.explanation: The Zagwe dynasty was plagued by internal succession rivalries, which anti-Zagwe factions exploited by branding the Agaw rulers 'illegitimate usurpers' who lacked Solomonic descent; Yekuno Amlak mobilized armed forces with the backing of church leaders like Abune Tekle Haymanot, defeated Yetbarek in Gaynt in 1270, and restored the 'Solomonic' dynasty.

questions.question: What was the regional geopolitical standing of the medieval Kingdom of Damot prior to the late 13th-century rise of the restored Solomonic dynasty?

options.text: It was an isolated agrarian chiefdom completely confined to the lowlands of Benishangul
It was a tributary province directly administered by the bishops of the Coptic Church in Alexandria

It was a dominant regional power situated south of the Abay River that defeated Zagwe expeditions, forced the Sultanate of Shewa to pay tribute, and prompted a Christian-Muslim alliance to contain its influence
It maintained an exclusive commercial monopoly over the Red Sea port of Adulis

questions.explanation: Located south of the Blue Nile (Abay), the powerful Kingdom of Damot defeated Zagwe armies, subjugated Muslim territories, and forced the Sultanate of Shewa into tributary status, prompting the Sultanate of Shewa and the newly established Christian state under Yekuno Amlak to form an alliance to counter its dominance.
